Traditional Rösti for Berchtoldstag

Served at: Berchtoldstag

Serves 4-6Prep 20 minCook 35 min

Rösti is a beloved Swiss potato dish, often described as a giant potato pancake, celebrated for its crispy exterior and tender interior. It's a comforting and hearty meal perfectly suited for Berchtoldstag on January 2nd, a holiday observed in many parts of Switzerland. After the New Year's festivities, a simple yet satisfying dish like Rösti provides warmth and tradition for family gatherings.

Ingredients

  • 2 pounds (about 1 kg) starchy potatoes (like Russet or Yukon Gold)
  • 4 tablespoons (60 ml) unsalted butter or clarified butter (or lard), divided
  • 1 teaspoon (5 ml) salt, or to taste
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 ml) freshly ground black pepper, or to taste

Method

  1. Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water until just tender when pierced with a fork, about 15-20 minutes depending on size. Do not overcook them until mushy. Drain well and let them cool completely, ideally refrigerating them overnight. Cold potatoes are crucial for the best texture.
  2. Once the potatoes are thoroughly chilled, peel them and grate them using the coarse side of a box grater.
  3. In a large bowl, gently toss the grated potatoes with salt and pepper until evenly seasoned.
  4. Heat a large (10-12 inch or 25-30 cm) heavy-bottomed non-stick or cast-iron skillet over medium heat. Add 2 tablespoons (30 ml) of the butter to the skillet and let it melt until shimmering.
  5. Add all the seasoned grated potatoes to the hot skillet. Using a spatula, press the potatoes down firmly and evenly to form a compact, flat cake. Do not stir or move the potatoes once pressed.
  6. Cook undisturbed for 15-20 minutes, or until a deep golden-brown and crispy crust forms on the bottom. You can gently lift an edge with a spatula to check the color.
  7. To flip the Rösti, place a large, flat plate over the skillet. Carefully and confidently invert the skillet onto the plate, so the Rösti rests on the plate, cooked side up. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons (30 ml) of butter to the skillet, let it melt.
  8. Carefully slide the Rösti from the plate back into the skillet, uncooked side down. Continue cooking for another 10-15 minutes, or until the second side is also deeply golden brown and crisp.
  9. Once both sides are golden and crispy, slide the Rösti onto a serving platter. Cut into wedges and serve immediately.

Tips

  • Using cold, day-old boiled potatoes is the secret to achieving the perfect crispy exterior and fluffy interior of traditional Rösti.
  • Don't skimp on the fat; it's essential for developing that delicious golden crust. Clarified butter or lard adds authentic flavor.
  • Rösti is versatile: serve it as a main dish with a fried egg, applesauce, or a dollop of sour cream, or as a hearty side dish to roasted meats.
